name: Durak Prostoy (Simple Durak)
description: Durak Prostoy (Simple Fool) is the archaic and most straightforward version of the Russian card game Durak. Predating the popular 'Podkidnoy' (throw-in) and 'Perevodnoy' (transfer) variants, it simplifies the interaction between players. In Prostoy, an attacker leads a card or a group of cards of the same rank, and the defender must either beat all of them or pick them up. There are no secondary attacks or throwing in of cards once the defense has begun, making for a faster, more linear game focused on card-for-card strength.

history.origins: Prostoy is the original form of Durak that emerged in the 18th century. It was the standard way the game was played until the late 19th century when the 'throw-in' (Podkidnoy) rules were introduced and eventually became the new standard.
timeline: 1700s: Durak Prostoy is documented in Russian royal courts and remote villages alike.
1850s: Modern variations begin to overshadow the Simple version.
Modern: Primarily played as a fast training variant or by children learning the basics of Russian beating games.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'grandparent' of Russian card games; it represents the simplest expression of the 'Fool' mechanic.
history.evolution: The transition from Prostoy to Podkidnoy marked the shift from individual card strength to tactical group collaboration.

setup.deck: 36-card Russian pack (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A).
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards, one at a time clockwise. The next card is placed face-up to determine the trump suit; the stock is placed face down on it.

rules.objective: Shed all cards. Do not be the last person remaining with cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Attacking: One player leads a single card or several cards of the SAME RANK.
2. Defending: The defender must beat all lead cards (higher card of same suit or trump).
3. Outcome: If beaten, the cards are discarded. If not, the defender picks them up.
4. Ending: No more cards can be added to the attack once the defender starts their defense.
keyRules: Only the cards played in the initial lead constitute the attack.
Players replenish their hands only after the defense is completely resolved.
If more than one card is led, they MUST be of the same rank (e.g., two 7s).

strategy.basic: Save your trumps for rounds where the attacker leads multi-card attacks of the same rank.
strategy.intermediate: Hand Management: Since there is no throwing-in, you can safely play high cards early to ensure you have a 'safe' exit once the deck is empty.
strategy.advanced: The Multi-Lead: If you have three of a kind, lead all three at once. This significantly increases the odds that the defender will be forced to pick up cards, given they must respond to all three in one go without the benefit of a sequential defense.
tips: In Prostoy, the attacker has a significant advantage in the lead because they can dictate the exact number of cards the defender must handle.
Count the trumps! Since the game is linear, knowing how many trumps remain is easier and more effective than in complex variations.
